The bakery on Halloway Street smelled of burnt sugar when Margaret Ashby-Lowe pushed the door open. Her brother Tom followed her in, shaking rain from his coat. A card in the window still read "OPEN" in faded red letters.

“We’re closed,” said the woman behind the counter, without looking up from her dough.

“The sign says you’re open,” Margaret said.

The woman sighed and set down her rolling pin. “Then the sign is wrong. Come back tomorrow.”

“We only need one loaf,” Tom said. “It’s for our mother’s birthday.”

The woman looked at him for a long moment. “One loaf. And you didn’t get it from me.”

Margaret laughed. “Thank you.”

Tom held the door for his sister on the way out. “You could have smiled at her,” he said.

Outside, Tom waited until their cousin Sam was watching, then threw him the loaf. “Catch,” he said.

Sam caught it against his chest. “Next time, warn me first.”
